protocol.measurement: Published SCB May val-idag estimate to September election; survey error plus campaign change.
protocol.closure: Each poll and election is closed to that panel's named parties; denominators differ across panels. OTHER and missing SD are never imputed.
protocol.historical_isotropic: Zero-mean isotropic CLR Gaussian; sigma^2=sum of squared training CLR residuals/(n*(p-1)).
protocol.historical_bias_shrunk_covariance: Training mean CLR error plus 50% sample covariance and 50% isotropic covariance in the CLR zero-sum subspace. Fixed shrinkage, not selected on test.
metrics: RMSE and MAE of ensemble-mean composition in percentage points
all-party joint coverage of those marginal intervals
protocol.selection: All declared models reported. No best model selected, no production profile changed, no post-test tuning.
protocol.vintage: Only original-release numbers transcribed from SCB publications/official SCB press accounts are admitted. The current Vid10 series retrospectively reweights 2010–2019 and is excluded.
protocol.zero_handling: Reject nonpositive or missing shares in a selected panel; do not add a pseudocount or invent a new-party history.
protocol.scope: Retrospective rolling-origin national-composition experiment; no full district election replay for newly added years, no prospective blind-validation or government-probability claim. Later outcomes in earlier training labels are necessary historical training data; target outcomes are used only for scoring.

revision_note.locator: Important footnotes: 2020 adjusted weighting, earlier results recomputed back to 2010; original published results available separately.
revision_note.consequence: Current-vintage 2010–2019 database values are not silently mixed with original-release values. Publication dates on today's documents do not establish independent historical real-time accessibility.

limitations: The seven-party panel excludes SD and OTHER; its scale is not the eight-party production scale. The panels are not scored against each other.
Missing/approximate SD points in 2002 and 2006 are not imputed. Eight-party coverage starts in 2010.
Seven/five elections and five/three rolling test elections remain a small, dependent historical sample. Parties are not independent elections.
May-to-September residuals combine survey error and campaign change. They are not election-day polling errors.
Original-release facts were transcribed from currently accessible official documents. Original downloaded bytes and independently archived historical real-time accessibility are not established.
SCB current Vid10 values for 2010–2019 were retrospectively revised after the 2020 weighting adjustment and are excluded from original-vintage training.
Historical data span changing poll methods, party systems and campaigning. Exchangeable residuals, Gaussian CLR form and fixed shrinkage are modeling assumptions.
Parameter uncertainty is not included in the intervals; small training samples can make them overconfident. Joint coverage refers to all marginal intervals, not a simultaneous-90% band.

This national-composition validation uses the declared CLR estimates without the native stress service sigma<=0.2 cap. Learned scales can exceed 0.2; they are not installed as valid native stress profiles.
Previously inspected 2022/2026 outcomes are development data, not new blind holdouts. No model is selected after these scores, and no production default is changed.
Newly added national vote counts do not validate full district allocations for 2002, 2006 or 2010.
